newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY MINISTRY SEES $2.5BLN 96 FOREIGN TRADE GAP.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY MINISTRY SEES $2.5BLN 96 FOREIGN TRADE GAP.

text.p: Hungary's foreign trade gap is likely to widen to some $2.5 billion by the end of this year, the upper limit of the country's target, the Ministry of Industry and Trade (IKM) said on Thursday.
"The foreign trade deficit will be around $2.5 billion," Lajos Berenyi, IKM Secretary of State told a news conference.
He added that Hungary had planned a trade gap of between $2 and 2.5 billion for this year.
IKM trade figures are calculated from customs statistics.
Berenyi said Hungary reduced its trade deficit to $2 billion in the first eight months of this year from $2.2 billion in the same period of 1995.
Exports rose by 3.8 percent to $8.3 billion, while imports increased by only 1.1 percent to $10.3 billion, he added.
In the January-August period, $1.4 billion of the trade gap contributed to the current account deficit, the IKM said.
This figure is likely to increase to some $1.5 billion by the end of 1996 but this still makes the $2 billion current account deficit target reachable, Berenyi said.

Hungary hoped to boost its exports by six to eight percent next year while trends in imports will depend on a upcoming government decision on the exact rate of pre-announced devaluations next year, he said.
The government said recently it would either retain the current 1.2 percent monthly devaluation rate or cut it.
Berenyi said exporters would favour an unchanged devaluation rate. He added he did not believe that keeping ot the same would endanger Hungary's 18 percent 1998 inflation target.
"The growth of consumer prices really declined at a slower pace this year than expected but producer prices fell more quickly," he said.
